title: Observation of Magnetic-Anisotropy Crossover and High-Temperature Skyrmions in the Dirac Magnet Fe3Ge with a Distorted Kagome Lattice
authors: Yalei Huang, Xiaowei Lv, Bin Li, Chunqiang Xu, Dhanarajagopal Alltrin, Xiaoxuan Ma, Wanting Yang, Wei Zhou, Xiangzhuo Xing, Wen-Chin Lin, Raman Sankar, Michael Smidman, Shixun Cao, Dong Qian, Renchao Che, Xiaofeng Xu
abstract: Topological materials that simultaneously host robust high-temperature skyrmions and nontrivial electronic band structures have attracted tremendous interest owing to their distinctive advantages for both fundamental research and prospective technological applications. Here, we report the observation of robust skyrmions in the Dirac kagome magnet Fe3Ge, which exhibits a high Curie temperature of ~ 650 K. At room temperature, Fe3Ge shows a large intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity of ~ 380 Ω-1cm-1, originating from its nontrivial electronic band topology. Systematic magnetization measurements reveal a spin reorientation transition at ~ 375 K, indicating a crossover from easy-plane to easy-axis magnetic anisotropy. Below the spin reorientation temperature, a large topological Hall effect is observed, arising from microscopic noncoplanar spin structures. Lorentz transmission electron microscopy shows that mesoscopic skyrmions are stabilized in the easy-axis magnetic anisotropy regime and persist over an exceptionally wide temperature window of 375-650 K, far exceeding that of most previously reported skyrmion-hosting materials. These results establish Fe3Ge as a promising platform for exploring diverse topological properties, with strong potential for advancing future high-temperature spintronic applications, ranging from next-generation information storage to logic computing devices.
summary: This work reports the discovery of robust, high-temperature skyrmions in the Dirac magnet $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{Ge}$. By analyzing magnetic anisotropy crossovers and topological transport measurements, the authors demonstrate that $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{Ge}$ maintains stable skyrmion phases up to its Curie temperature ($\sim 650 	ext{ K}$). This positions the material as a leading candidate for advanced spintronic applications.
main_problem: The study investigates the interplay between magnetic anisotropy, electronic band topology, and the stability of skyrmions in the Dirac magnet $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{Ge}$.
main_result: The authors report observing robust skyrmions in $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{Ge}$ that persist over a wide temperature range (375 K to 650 K), establishing it as a promising platform for high-temperature spintronics.
method: The research combines experimental techniques like Lorentz TEM and magneto-transport measurements with theoretical calculations using methods like FPLAPW.
model_or_system: The physical system is the $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{Ge}$ single crystal, which possesses a distorted Kagome lattice and exhibits Dirac magnetic properties. The analysis focuses on the magnetic phase transitions and the resulting topological electronic structure.
key_observables: High Curie temperature ($\sim 650 	ext{ K}$), large intrinsic Anomalous Hall Conductivity ($\sim 380 \ \Omega^{-1}	ext{cm}^{-1}$), Spin Reorientation Transition ($\sim 375 	ext{ K}$), and stable mesoscopic skyrmions.
important_parameters: Temperature range (375 K to 650 K), magnetic anisotropy constants ($K_{	ext{eff}}$), and the material's intrinsic electronic topology.
main_assumptions: The electronic structure is linked to nontrivial band topology, and the magnetic behavior is governed by the crossover between easy-plane and easy-axis anisotropy.
